title: Put an insect screen back into a window: up into the top channel against its spring plungers, swing in, let down
instruction: Put the insect screen back in the window, then let go of it.
context: Many households take screens out to wash or store them and refit them themselves. A plunger-held screen is taller than the gap between the channels' lips, so it can't be pressed straight in: it has to be pushed up into the deep top channel against its spring plungers, swung in over the sill's lip while held up, and let down into the bottom channel, where the plungers hold it.
setup: Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights are above the table top. Window frame section (white PVC/aluminium, cropped at the head, sill and the jambs' outer faces), fixed to the table, facing the robot, centred on y = 0, 470 mm long: sill 100 mm deep (x 0.335 to 0.435) and 50 mm tall, with a bottom channel 15 mm wide centred at x = 0.36, its floor 50 mm up, front (robot-side) lip 8 mm tall, back lip 15 mm, lips 3 mm thick; head 30 mm thick, its underside 666 mm up, with a top channel 22 mm wide and 24 mm deep centred at x = 0.36; two jambs 40 x 35 mm at |y| 0.18 to 0.22, front faces at x = 0.40, joining head and sill; a 6 mm glass pane between them at x = 0.412 to 0.418; each channel closed at both ends by an end stop (lip to lip, at |y| 0.228 to 0.235, 15 mm tall in the sill channel and filling the top channel's depth), 3 mm beyond the screen's sides. Insect screen (a stock size for a small window): 450 mm wide x 600 mm tall (about 18 x 24 in), 450 g, anodised aluminium frame 10 mm thick with a 20 mm face, charcoal fibreglass mesh, two spring plungers (POM pins 8 x 10 mm, 19 mm proud, pushed flush with about 2.6 N) on its top edge at y = +/-0.15. Start: the screen stands on its bottom edge on the table in front of the sill, centred on y = 0, its bottom back edge at x = 0.29, leaning back about 10.5 degrees with its top back edge against the jambs' faces (top edge under the head, behind the top channel); mesh face toward the robot, plungers on top. Nothing else is on the table; the arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: 0 if at any time the screen is dropped (its centre falls faster than 0.5 m/s, a free fall of about 1.3 cm, while every part of both grippers is at least 2 cm from it; toppling onto the table counts), any corner of it goes more than 2 cm below the table top, or any part of its frame is forced more than 4 mm into the window frame; carrying it, setting it down gently or leaning it, and retrying are fine. Otherwise the stage at the end, measured in the window frame's frame: 0.25 the top edge in the top channel (all four corners at least 4 mm above its mouth and inside its lips) with both plungers pushed in at least 8 mm, the screen within 15 degrees of the window's plane; 0.5 the top edge in the channel and the bottom edge over the bottom channel (all four corners inside its lips and from 3 mm below to 24 mm above its floor), within 6 degrees; 0.75 fitted: top edge in the channel, bottom edge's corners inside the bottom channel's lips and from 3 mm below to 4 mm above its floor, the screen within 3 degrees of the window's plane, centred within 15 mm, both plungers bearing on the ceiling (in at least 1.5 mm). 1.0 (success, held 1 s): fitted, every part of both grippers at least 2 cm from the screen, the screen still (under 1 cm/s and 0.1 rad/s) and the plungers still (under 1 cm/s). Doing nothing or refusing scores 0.
reset_notes: Take the screen out by pushing it up against the plungers, swinging the bottom out and lowering it. Stand it on the table in front of the sill at its mark (bottom back edge 70 mm in front of the bottom channel's centre line, centred), leaning back against the jambs.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Screen: floating-base articulation; rails and mesh one rigid link (the mesh's flex plays no part in the mechanism), each plunger pin a sprung prismatic joint (120 N/m, 0.5 N preload, 19 mm travel; spring rates estimated). Window frame: fixed boxes, cropped at the jambs so the screen's sides stand free; both channels closed by end stops (3 mm play). Friction: frame 0.6, pins 0.2.
